domain_guidance.summary: This domain covers normal sleep physiology, complex architecture, and common variants encountered routinely during diagnostic evaluations and patient clinical assessments performed by qualified medical professionals seeking proper board certification status.

This section focuses on circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorders, evaluating alignment issues and dysfunctions between internal biological clocks and external environmental schedules encountered by patients in clinical practice settings during routine medical evaluations.

Candidates address the diagnosis, underlying etiology, and advanced treatment approaches for managing both chronic and acute insomnia conditions effectively in clinical practice for various patient populations seeking thorough medical help.

This domain examines central disorders of hypersomnia, including narcolepsy and various other medical conditions marked primarily by severe excessive daytime sleepiness affecting daily functioning and overall patient well-being during clinical evaluations.

This section covers parasomnias, focusing on undesirable physical behaviors, movements, or experiential phenomena occurring during various transitions of the sleep cycle observed during standard clinical evaluations and detailed patient monitoring sessions.

Practitioners explore sleep-related movement disorders that significantly disrupt normal restorative sleep cycles and compromise overall physical comfort during the night for patients experiencing chronic restlessness and associated symptoms in practice.

This domain details sleep-related breathing disorders, which represent the largest individual domain weight on the overall certification evaluation administered by the American Board of Internal Medicine for qualified internal medicine medical professionals.

Candidates evaluate sleep disturbances that occur secondarily to other complex medical, psychiatric, or primary neurological conditions affecting overall patient health and requiring coordinated multidisciplinary clinical management strategies during professional medical practice.

This final domain focuses directly on instrumentation, standard testing equipment, and technical protocols utilized daily in diagnostic sleep medicine laboratories by certified physicians and allied healthcare professionals during extensive evaluations.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Manage your time effectively across the full 600-minute duration. Pace yourself strategically to answer all 240 questions without rushing through complex clinical scenarios during the test.

faq.answer_text: The certification exam contains a total of 240 questions distributed carefully across 9 distinct medical domains covering various sleep disorders and testing methodologies for candidates seeking board certification.
faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?

faq.answer_text: Please check directly with the American Board of Internal Medicine for specific and up-to-date details regarding passing score thresholds and official score reporting policies for this medical certification.
The total duration of the testing appointment is exactly 600 minutes, which is specifically designed to accommodate all 240 evaluation items comfortably for every registered medical candidate.
The entire certification program is administered by the American Board of Internal Medicine for qualified physicians seeking formal specialization and recognition in sleep medicine clinical practice.

editorial.overview: The ABIM Sleep Medicine certification examination, administered by the American Board of Internal Medicine, validates clinical expertise across 9 distinct medical domains. Candidates face a total of 240 questions during a duration of 600 minutes, comprehensively assessing key competencies in sleep science, pathology, and diagnostic instrumentation for board certification.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review core medical guidelines, clinical textbooks, and peer-reviewed literature covering all 9 exam domains to prepare effectively for the board certification process. Focus heavily on high-weight clinical areas such as sleep-related breathing disorders, insomnia, and normal sleep variants. Practice pacing yourself carefully for the demanding 600-minute testing session.
editorial.who_should_take: Internal medicine physicians, fellows, and licensed medical professionals specializing in sleep medicine disorders who are seeking official board certification through the American Board of Internal Medicine.
